extracted.intended_audience: students and teachers of mathematics; general problem solvers interested in mathematical heuristics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and heuristics for solving mathematical problems (Pólya's method): understanding the problem, devising and carrying out a plan, and reviewing/extension; includes many specific heuristics for constructing or transforming problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the problem
rubrics_metrics.description: First step: ensure you truly understand what is being asked before attempting a solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompting questions: What are you asked to find or show? Can you restate the problem in your own words? Can you think of a picture or diagram that might help? Is there enough information? Do you understand all the words used? Do you need to ask a question to get the answer? Teachers should select questions at appropriate difficulty for each student and keep prompting until the student can respond constructively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devise a plan
rubrics_metrics.description: After understanding, make a plan — choose an appropriate strategy to solve the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are many reasonable strategies; skill at choosing one improves with practice. Applying rules to devise a plan requires judgement. Teachers should support students in devising their own plans by questioning from general to particular so the final step is made by the student rather than simply showing a solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carry out the plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Execute the chosen plan carefully and patiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This step is often easier than devising the plan. Persist with chosen plan; if it fails, discard it and choose another. Care and patience and required skills are essential; professionals also change strategies when misled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Look back / Review and extend
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflect on the solution and its method; consider improvements and extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze what worked and what didn't, think about other problems where the method applies, and use this reflection to predict strategies for future related problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher question-method support
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers should guide students through problem solving using a sequence of targeted questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a hierarchy of questions from general to specific to help students understand and devise plans at their own level. Avoid merely showing the plan; the goal is student-generated planning. Select the appropriate question level for each student and adapt as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guess and check
rubrics_metrics.description: Try candidate solutions and test them until one works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for problems where plausible guesses can be generated and verified quickly; part of Pólya's partial strategy list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make an orderly list
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematically list possibilities or cases to search for a solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organized enumeration helps ensure completeness and can reveal structure or patterns; useful when the search space is manageable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate possibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule out impossible or inconsistent cases to narrow the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prune the space of candidates by logical exclusion; often used together with ordered listing or symmetry arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploit symmetrical structure in the problem to simplify or reduce cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symmetry can reduce complexity by identifying equivalent cases or invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine easier or boundary cases to gain insight about the general problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special cases can suggest patterns or expose pitfalls; useful both for understanding and constructing a plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use direct reasoning / Solve an equation / Use a formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply straightforward logical deduction or algebraic manipulation (set up and solve equations, apply known formulas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, direct analytic methods are efficient; recognize when a problem reduces to standard algebraic or formulaic computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Look for a pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: Search for recurring structure or regularity among examples or cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pattern detection can lead to conjectures, generalizations, or formulas; often a prelude to induction or general solution methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draw a picture / Diagrammatic reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent the problem visually to reveal relationships not obvious from the statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagrams often make structure explicit and can suggest constructions or simplifications; Pólya emphasizes drawing figures as a heuristic (formal analogue: diagrammatic reasoning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Solve a simpler problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Find and solve a related problem that is easier, then use its solution to approach the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplification can provide insight or a building block; Pólya suggests trying more accessible related problems when the original resists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a model
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a concrete or physical model that captures the essential features of the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models can make abstract relationships tangible and reveal solution paths; they are helpful pedagogically and for individual problem solving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work backward (backward chaining)
rubrics_metrics.description: Start from the desired conclusion and reason backward to known facts or simpler goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with the goal and deduce what must be true earlier; often reveals a chain of necessary subgoals leading to known conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply known identities, theorems or formulas directly when the problem matches a standard form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize opportunities to deploy standard results to simplify or complete the solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be creative
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ original or non-standard ideas when routine strategies fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creativity is an acknowledged strategy; cultivating inventive approaches comes with practice and exposure to varied problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogy
rubrics_metrics.description: Find an analogous problem that you can solve and transfer the method or insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal analogue noted as 'map' — map elements of a solved analogous problem to the current one to adapt the solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auxiliary elements / Extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Add new elements (variables, constructions, parameters) to the problem to make it easier to solve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introducing auxiliary lines, points, functions, or parameters can bridge the gap to a solution (formal analogue: extension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace the problem by a more general one whose solution implies the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solving a more general problem can simplify reasoning or reveal structural properties (formal analogue: generalization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Induction
rubrics_metrics.description: Derive a general result from patterns observed in examples and prove by induction where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examples to conjecture a general rule, then use mathematical induction or analogous general proof techniques (formal analogue: induction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Variation of the problem (search)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alter or vary the problem to create related problems whose solutions help solve the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploring variations can expose solvable relatives or reveal invariant aspects; the formal analogue listed is 'search'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auxiliary problem / Subgoal
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and solve subproblems or side problems whose solutions contribute to the main problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decompose into subgoals that are easier to handle; solving these can combine into a solution for the original (formal analogue: subgoal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a previously solved related problem (pattern matching)
rubrics_metrics.description: Locate a problem already solved that relates to the current one and adapt its solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pattern recognition: match structural similarities to import methods or results from solved instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction / Specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce the problem to a more specialized or simpler instance that is easier to solve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specializing parameters or reducing generality can lead to solvable cases; then lift the solution or use it as a building block.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposing and recombining (divide and conquer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Break the problem into parts, solve each, and recombine solutions to form the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decomposition isolates manageable pieces; recombination may require creative assembly or auxiliary arguments (formal analogue: divide and conquer).
